topic.name: Geography Lesson
topic.description: Zulfikar Ghose's poem describes how a city looks from a jet climbing higher and higher -- neat and logical from the air where it looked haphazard on the ground -- and ends on the one thing that height cannot explain: why people on earth build walls and kill each other.

concepts.name: Zulfikar Ghose, the poet
concepts.description: The poem is signed with its poet's name directly beneath the final stanza.
concepts.definition: The poem 'Geography Lesson' is written by Zulfikar Ghose.

concepts.name: Six inches to the mile
concepts.description: As the jet climbs, the city is scaled down to six inches to the mile, and what looked haphazard on the ground now shows an inevitability about how it had developed.
concepts.definition: When the jet sprang into the sky, the city was seen scaled six inches to the mile, and it became clear why it had developed as it had.
concepts.source_evidence: Seeing it Scaled Six inches ४० the mile

concepts.name: Inevitable and haphazard, glossed
concepts.description: The poem's own glossary defines inevitable as that which cannot be avoided, and haphazard as without plan or order -- the two words the first stanza turns on.
concepts.definition: Inevitable means that cannot be avoided; haphazard means without plan or order.
concepts.source_evidence: inevitable. that cannot be avoided Haphazard: Without plan ०r Order

concepts.name: The logic of geography
concepts.description: At ten thousand feet it becomes clear why cities have grown where rivers run and why valleys are populated: land and water attracted man, and that is what the poem calls the logic of geography.
concepts.definition: The logic of geography is that land and water attracted man, which is why cities followed rivers and valleys were populated.
concepts.source_evidence: The logic of geography that Iand and Water Attracted man

concepts.name: Six miles high, the earth is round
concepts.description: At six miles the jet rises high enough for the curve of the earth to become visible, and for it to be clear that the earth holds more sea than land.
concepts.definition: When the jet rose six miles high, it became clear that the earth was round and that it had more sea than land.
concepts.source_evidence: It Was Clear the earth Was round And that it had more Sea than Iand

concepts.name: Why men find causes to kill
concepts.description: The one thing height cannot make clear: why the men on the earth find causes to hate each other, build walls across cities, and kill.
concepts.definition: From that height, it was not clear why the men on the earth found causes to hate each other, build walls across cities, and kill.
concepts.source_evidence: the men ०n the earth ound Causes ४० hate each Other
